hint.text: A species is a group of living things that are very similar and can reproduce with each other.
hint.label: Species

feedback.end: Speciation is when new species are formed. This often happens when a population becomes separated, resulting in two or more new species forming over time.

atoms.text: This picture shows the stages of speciation.

instruction.text: Use the picture to sort the stages of speciation into the correct order.

atoms.text: There is one large population living together.
The population becomes separated by a physical barrier.
The two separate populations adapt to their new environments and have their own offspring.
Over time, two new species evolve.

instruction.text: Here are two owls that evolved from one common ancestor. Select the difference between them.

atoms.b: Mexican spotted owls and northern spotted owls evolved from a common ((++ancestor person)) that became separated by mountains and deserts.
Mexican spotted owls live in a warmer climate in the south, so evolved to have ((++lighter colourful)) feathers to camouflage with the trees there.
The trees in the north are ((++darker softer)), so northern spotted owls evolved to have darker feathers with smaller white spots.
